Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply online now Come to an Open Day Start date September 2027 Location Blended learning Cambridge Chelmsford UCAS course code L501 Duration 3 years 1st in the region for graduates progressing into senior roles. Source: GOS 2026 Social work changes lives. This challenging yet rewarding career will often bring you into the lives of some of the most disadvantaged and marginalised communities. It’s a complex job that demands many soft skills, such as communication and partnership working. As a student at ARU, you’ll learn how to assess people’s circumstances and needs; measure risk; and provide services and interventions. You’ll develop your skills out on placement, and graduate with a nationally recognised qualification. Social Work England Our course is approved by Social Work England. When you graduate, you'll be eligible to apply to register as a professional social worker. Hear from Deputy Head of School for Social Work in Chelmsford, Jenny Rafter Close full-screen gallery. Hear from Deputy Head of School for Social Work in Chelmsford, Jenny Rafter Why ARU? Learn from expert academics who bring insights from various professional social work backgrounds Work with educators who support your social work learning with their lived experience of services Receive dedicated support with resources focused on your wellbeing and academic growth Gain real-world experience through placements, preparing you for diverse social work settings Graduate from an accredited course and apply for registration to start your career Explore flexible career options in community work, healthcare and child welfare Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers I have always wanted to work with young people in care… Training as a social worker has helped me understand my own experiences. Cassie Solola, BSc (Hons) Social Work graduate Our degree course is a professional qualification, approved by Social Work England. Social workers must be registered and, once you finish this course, you’ll be able to apply to register with Social Work England. During your time with us, you'll gain the skills and knowledge you need for a career as a social worker. You’ll be skilled in case management and able to work safely within the law. What can you do with a Social Work degree? Once you’re registered there’s a wide range of job opportunities for trained social workers. Our graduates work in services including adoption, fostering, child protection, adult safeguarding and youth offending. You can choose to work in the public, private or voluntary sectors – often alongside colleagues from other disciplines. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? Our students and alumni go on to do great work - see here Solomon Tugbiyele ( Student Social Worker of the Year 2022 winner), and Newly Qualified Social Worker of the Year 2022 shortlistees Dawn Bedwell (Children's) and Sehrish Zeb (Adult). We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules This practical course has a strong focus on placements, and you’ll spend a total of 170 days on placement in Years 2 and 3. While on placement, you’ll be working directly with people accessing services under the supervision of a qualified social worker. In university, we’ll look at some of the reasons why people may come into contact with social workers – for example poverty, inequality or social exclusion – and the signs of abuse and neglect. There’s also a strong focus on social work with adults, and with children and families. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Applied Social Work Theories Contemporary Issues in Social Work Safeguarding in Context Standards and Skills for Social Work Practice 1 Into ARU Year 2 Social Work with Children and Families Standards and Skills for Social Work Practice 2 Social Work with Adults Research - Evaluating Knowledge and Evidence in Practice Can We Work Together to Safeguard Vulnerable Families? * Do we know what it takes to be an Anti-Racist? * What does it mean to be a feminist? * Rise of the Peterborians - can we create positive change * Year 3 Wellbeing - A Life Course Perspective Understanding Professional Practice Undergraduate Major Project Standards and Skills for Social Work Practice 3 Module details What happens during a placement? During your Social Work degree, you’ll spend 170 days out on placement. All of our students do two practice placements: 70 days in Year 2, and 100 days in Year 3. You’ll benefit from: the chance to learn from registered social workers covering both adults and children experience of working in different settings experience of working directly with people accessing services. Both placements are an invaluable opportunity to learn in the workplace and you’ll cover a range of topics such as engagement, assessment, interpersonal skills, interventions, safeguarding and the appropriate use of authority. One of your placements will involve statutory tasks, including legal interventions. We’ll make sure that you get a range of settings to best support your training. If you study in Chelmsford, your placements could be anywhere in Essex, including Thurrock and Southend, and/or with placement providers in neighbouring areas. If you're joining us in Cambridge, your placements could be anywhere in Cambridgeshire and/or with placement providers in neighbouring areas. It’s likely that you’ll have to travel as part of your placement, so you’ll need your own transport to visit people in areas where public transport may not be available. Driving requirement for placement If you don’t drive or have a car, please keep in mind how this might affect your placement options. Some 70-day placements might be accessible, but for your 100-day/final placement, local authorities and statutory placement providers will not accept non-driving students due to the need for timely fieldwork, like home visits and accessing county-wide located services. Placements may also involve travel up to 1.5 hours from the university campus you’re studying at. If you live outside East Anglia we’ll try to find a placement closer to you but this cannot be guaranteed. What you'll learn on placement First placement (70 days) You’ll have an opportunity to integrate theory and practice in your assessment and intervention when working with individuals, families, carers, groups or communities. You’ll be able to reflect upon your own values and beliefs and confront any conflict with the principles and values underpinning social work practice, with guided supervision. There are opportunities to advocate for what is in the best interests of the service user, promoting service user voice and encouraging their independent choices. You'll undertake tasks such as interviewing service users to gather information, reviewing care plans, undertaking home visits, and needs versus risk assessments to promote relationship-based practice. You’ll be guided to develop and understand the process of critical reflection and evaluation as a tool for improving professional practice. Second placement (100 days) You’ll undertake more complex tasks to demonstrate your developing knowledge, skills and values. Tasks can include completing a single assessment or life story work if working in a children’s team, or undertaking a Mental Capacity Act (2005) assessment if working in an adults' team. We'll assign much longer pieces of work to deepen and sharpen your social work skills in readiness for qualifying as a social worker. You’ll engage with assessment, intervention and the management of risk within complex situations. You'll also develop an ability to manage and be accountable for your own social work practice in an organisational setting, making competent use of supervision and support. Support you'll have on placement There is a dedicated placements team that will work closely with you to plan for both placements. Practice Educator (PE) You’ll be assigned a Practice Educator to support you during your training and assess your practice over the duration of the placement. PEs are social workers trained in the teaching and assessment of students on practice placements. They meet the Practice Educator Professional Standards (PEPS) and their role is to support you in integrating theory and knowledge from university into practice. They are responsible for the assessment of your practice. Placement Tutor (PT) Your Placement Tutor will also be a critical support person for you on placement. They are a member of the university. Most of our placement tutors are academics within the Social Work team, so you’ll know them. The PT will attend meetings at the placement site to ensure that the placement is set up in a way that’ll meet your learning needs and the University’s requirements. They're also there to support you if you have any difficulties during the placement. Your PT is your first point of contact for all placement-related matters. How is BA (Hons) Social Work assessed? We use a number of assessment methods including assignments, role-plays, presentations, practice portfolios and placements. Assessments are your opportunity to show the skills and knowledge that you're gaining. Placements provide you with the opportunity to work towards meeting the requirements of the Professional Standards and the Knowledge and Skills Statements. You'll need to pass both placements, alongside all academic modules, in order to qualify for registration as a Social Worker with Social Work England. Who teaches Social Work at ARU? Undergraduate BSc (Hons) Nursing (Children) Prepare for a fulfilling career as a nurse for babies, children and young people with our accredited degree course. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Come to an Open Day BSc (Hons) With foundation year BSc (Hons) Start date September 2027 Location Cambridge Chelmsford King's Lynn Peterborough UCAS course code B730 Duration 3 years With foundation year Start date January 2027 September 2027 Location Cambridge Chelmsford Peterborough UCAS course code B732 Duration 4 years with foundation Clearing availability You can apply to start the four-year course, which includes a foundation year, in 2026. Notes on Peterborough foundation year Progression from this foundation year into Level 4 of the NMC approved degree course requires a successful interview, DBS check and occupational health clearance. The Peterborough foundation year is not NMC approved. 2nd in England for undergraduates progressing into full-time employment or full-time further study. Source: GOS 2026 (subjects allied to medicine) Accommodation guarantee and commuter support Guaranteed accommodation for Cambridge, Chelmsford and Writtle starters, and support for commuting students. Apply by 25 September Nursing really is a job for life. As a child nurse, you’ll make a difference to many people’s lives, including your own. Study at ARU and gain the clinical knowledge, skills and confidence you need to succeed as a registered children’s nurse. As well as developing your clinical skills, you’ll learn to communicate with young patients and their families, advocate for them, and place wellbeing at the centre of the care you deliver. Nursing & Midwifery Council Our Nursing degree courses are validated by the NMC and you’ll be linked to one of our eight NHS healthcare trust partners for your placements. This is ARU Nursing students speaking for themselves — no filter, just an honest take on what the course is really like. Close full-screen gallery. This is ARU Nursing students speaking for themselves — no filter, just an honest take on what the course is really like. Why ARU? Gain practical experience with 50% clinical placements in healthcare settings. Get relevant, up-to-date training thanks to our partnerships with NHS Trusts. Build your clinical skills in state-of-the-art simulation suites. Benefit from wellbeing support, academic guidance, and career services. Get a minimum of £5,000 per year non-repayable training grant. Graduate ready to work as a registered children's nurse. Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers I had always wanted a career that was rewarding and enabled me to make a difference to other people’s lives. Abbi, Child nursing student As a graduate, you'll be ready to work as a registered children's nurse. Our degree course is approved by the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) in the UK, meaning you’ll be eligible to apply for registration with them when you graduate – and start your career in nursing. Over 90% of our students have gone on to work or study, 15 months after their course (source: Discover Uni ). What can you do with a child nursing degree? Specialist children’s nurses can build careers in a variety of fields. You may choose to become a specialist nurse practitioner, a consultant nurse or a modern matron. Or you could specialise in a particular area such as health visiting or school nursing. Alternatively, you could take your education further with a post-registration course, conduct research or go into healthcare management . Teaching and modules If you teach what you love, they'll love what you teach. Sarah Scapens, Lecturer This is a highly practical course featuring placements from Year 1, so you can hone your practical skills. You'll explore the fundamentals of person-centred care, common and long-term health conditions, and how to assess and treat seriously ill patients. We'll learn how nurses can promote health and wellbeing, too. Crucially, you’ll also learn about good communication and working with families and carers. What will I study? BSc (Hons) With foundation year BSc (Hons) Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Into ARU Foundations of Communication and Professionalismfor Nursing Fundamental Skills and Procedures for Nursing Applied Health Science for Nursing Across the Lifespan Epidemiology, Inequality, and Health Promotion for Nursing Across the Lifespan Contemporary Nursing Practice 1 Year 2 Supporting a Patient Safety Culture in Nursing Supporting Learning and Professional Development in Nursing Contemporary Nursing Practice 2 Assessing and Planning Care Across the Lifespan Coordinating and Leading Integrated Care in Interprofessional Settings Year 3 Clinical Decision Making in the Acutely Unwell Child and Young Person Applying public health to children and young people’s nursing Contemporary Children and Young People’s Nursing Practice 3 Leading and managing quality in the care of children and young people Managing the Care of Children and Young People with Complex Care Needs Module details With foundation year To prepare you for university study, you can take a foundation year at the start of this course. Find out more about foundation years . 4 years with foundation Year 1 Cambridge, Chelmsford Core Maths Biology: Physiology Preparing for a Career in Caring Learning to Learn Psychology Embracing Diversity Health and Wellbeing Module details 4 years with foundation Peterborough Year 1 Peterborough Foundations of Health Across the Life Course Introduction to Life Sciences Literacies in Higher Education Module details What happens during placements? Our child nursing degree places equal value on clinical practice and theory – and you’ll spend 50% of your learning time on placement. You’ll be required to have DBS and occupational health clearance, including all your vaccinations, and to have completed all mandatory training and induction sessions before you can go on placement. Placements are a great chance to get hands-on experience in providing nursing care, and assessing, treating and communicating with patients. You may find yourself working at a GP surgery; in a variety of hospital settings, from A&E through to acute care and oncology; or working with a community team. With services being delivered remotely, we have placements integrating digital health and with virtual wards and teams. We also have virtual placements, where you can focus on the fundamental elements of nursing care in a safe, supportive environment, but access this from a home computer. Some virtual placements are delivered by practice partners, who work with us to ensure that the placement develops your knowledge and skills, and provides time for reflection and active discussion. Other virtual placements are delivered by ARU staff. Each placement lasts around 4 - 10 weeks and you will have experience in both the acute and community settings during the course. There are opportunities in older person care, dementia care, community nursing, social care, surgical and medical setting, virtual wards and more. There’s also the option of a self-funded overseas placement at the end of Year 2. While on placement, you’ll be working shifts, averaging 37.5 hours per week. This can mean early, late and night shifts, as well as weekends and bank holidays. You’ll be supported by practice supervisors and assessors as well as staff from ARU. You’ll be required to follow the uniform policy at University and on placement. In many clinical areas, in order to minimise the risk of infection, clothing is not permitted below the elbows. Please talk to one of our tutors about this if you have questions or would like more information. We’ll expect you to provide personal care to male, female and transgender patients. Each year, you’ll get allocated annual leave at set points to support you in balancing your course and relaxation time. These weeks may not coincide with school holidays. Our placement maps will help you plan your travel before you start on the course. What will I learn on placement? We want to make sure you experience a variety of placements and that you graduate as an effective practitioner. To meet the NMC standards, you will require practice learning opportunities to enable you to develop the skills to deliver safe and effective care to a diverse range of people. Nurses must be able to care for people in their own home, in the community or hospital or any health care setting, and you will experience a range of placements during the course. Your learning on placement will cover the required platforms: Being an accountable professional Promoting health and preventing ill health Assessing needs and planning care Providing and evaluating care Leading and managing nursing care and working in teams Improving safety and quality of care Coordinating care You will also gain experience in the required communication and relationship management skills, and nursing procedures. Examples of nursing procedures include: Undertaking a history and accurately assess people of all ages. Undertaking a whole-body systems assessment including respiratory, circulatory, neurological, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular and skin status. Assessing mental and physical health and wellbeing status Undertake venepuncture and cannulation and blood sampling, interpreting normal and common abnormal blood profiles and venous blood gases. Undertake chest auscultation and interpret findings Use of contemporary nutritional assessment tools Managing the administration of IV fluids Observe, assess and respond to potential infection risks using best practice guidelines Assess and review preferences and care priorities of the dying person and their family and carers Exercise professional accountability in ensuring the safe administration of medicines to those receiving care Where will I go on placements? You’ll be linked to one of our NHS healthcare trust partners for your placements, and have additional placements virtually or in health and social care settings. if you study in Cambridge or Peterborough, you’ll do your placements in or around Cambridge, Huntingdon or Peterborough if you study in Chelmsford, you’ll do your placements in or around Chelmsford, Southend, Basildon, Harlow or Colchester. This course also includes opportunities for international placements, which are a great way to broaden your perspectives of healthcare. There’s the option of a self-funded overseas placement with Work the World during Year 2. We make every effort to minimise the travelling distance involved but you may have to travel some distance to your placement. It is your responsibility to plan your journey and make sure you are on time for your shifts. Placement maps Nursing placements take place in these areas, depending on the nursing subject you choose and the campus you study at. To make sure you’re developing the skills and knowledge needed for professional practice, we use a range of assessment methods. These include essays, presentations, exams, case studies, project work and assessment of practice competencies in the clinical setting. We know feedback is essential for your progress and our lecturers take pride in giving you clear guidance on how to improve your expertise. What equipment will I need? Books An electronic tablet to access course content and undertake assessment in the practice setting Sensible shoes (as per uniform policy) Fob watch Who teaches Nursing (Children) at ARU? At ARU, you’ll learn in small, supportive group sessions led by our highly experienced staff. They’ll also offer support while you’re on placement, along with your practice supervisors and assessors. You’ll use sophisticated equipment to simulate many aspects of a working hospital ward. You’ll also learn from registered, practising tutors and lecturers who’ll make sure you’re being taught the latest techniques and give you the support you need to succeed. Applications and interviews Applying All applications must go via UCAS. We accept applications between September and January for the following intake year. Late applications will be considered if places are available. We do not accept applications or references from recruitment agencies or educational consultancies for Home (UK) students. References must be provided directly by an employer or academic referee. Interviews If your application is shortlisted we'll invite you to attend an interview: find out more about how you can prepare . We'll ask you to present some ID for verification checks. This can be a passport, driving licence, or ID badge from your current employer or college. Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) An enhanced level Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) disclosure is a check with police forces and local authorities in the UK to ascertain whether or not you are suitable to work with certain groups of vulnerable people. These checks are required to be carried out on all prospective students to ensure the safety of our client group. As a student, you will be required to undergo DBS screening each year. Further information on DBS disclosure will be sent at a later date if you are successful and firmly accept your place at ARU. Transferring to ARU We welcome applications into Year 2 of our BSc (Hons) Adult Nursing degree. You can apply through UCAS (or directly to us in Clearing which runs from July-September). We'll need to check that we can map your Year 1 studies to professional requirements and our own modules. You can study with us in Cambridge or Chelmsford, and start your course in September or March. When you apply, you'll need to provide: a transcript of your Year 1 study. This should show that you've successfully passed all Year 1 theory and practice modules and achieved all the practice hours. We cannot accept transcripts where marks are missing from Year 1 the module learning outcomes from each module you completed in Year 1 an academic reference from your previous place of study a personal statement of up to 500 words, explaining why you wish to transfer to ARU. Meeting the entry requirements If you don’t meet our advertised entry requirements, you could consider taking a foundation year. In Cambridge and Chelmsford you can join our Nursing Foundation Pathway . This is offered by ARU College. In Peterborough, you can take a foundation year before progressing to the Nursing (Child) or Nursing (Adult) degrees that are taught at ARU Peterborough. This initial year provides the academic, professional, and practical grounding needed to progress onto a BSc (Hons) Nursing degree at ARU. While the foundation year is not NMC-accredited, it offers an important stepping stone into fully accredited programmes by developing essential skills and confidence. It’s designed for those without traditional qualifications but who demonstrate potential through work experience or alternative study routes. During the foundation year, you’ll have the opportunity to apply for interview, and if successful, you’ll receive a conditional offer to progress, subject to completing Year 1 and meeting all requirements. Source: GOS 2026 Bring characters, performances and digital worlds to life with our BA (Hons) 3D Animation degree. You’ll build core skills in animation, character creation, visual storytelling and 3D production, then explore real-time tools and collaborative workflows used across games and wider creative industries. Through practical projects, you can develop your own specialism, create distinctive portfolio work and prepare for careers spanning animation, games, virtual production, VFX and digital content. Why ARU? Bring characters to life through animation, performance and visual storytelling. Combine 3D animation with real-time tools and games production workflows. Learn collaboratively in our £2.5 million next-generation games development studio environment. Explore motion capture, 3D scanning and specialist digital production technology. Develop your own specialism through increasingly independent creative projects. Build portfolio work and industry connections through feedback, talks and our annual Gamebridge . Designed for creative life Our Creative Quarter brings together studios, workshops, performance and exhibition spaces. Be part of a community built around making, experimentation and innovation, while developing your practical skills and portfolio, and connecting with industry. Careers Gain the skills to land a career in the gaming industry, and open doors to other sectors, including VFX, film, animation, television and motion graphics. Build a professional portfolio as you study, including an online presence on portfolio sites, websites and blogs, so you’re ready to showcase your skills to future employers and clients. You'll gain practical experience with industry-standard tools, software and production pipelines. The technical and creative skills you develop will open up opportunities across games, virtual production, VFX, film and animation, and the wider creative technology sector where experience with professional workflows and production pipelines is highly valued. What can you do with a 3D Animation degree? Your combination of animation, 3D production and real-time skills can take you beyond a single sector. You could go on to work in animation studios, games companies, VFX, virtual production, film and television, visualisation, advertising and digital content production. Possible roles include as 3D Animator, Character Animator, Layout Artist, Previsualisation Artist, Realtime Artist, Junior Technical Animator, Motion Capture Assistant, Visual Development Artist, Junior 3D Generalist, and Digital Content Creator. Where can 3D Animation students find work experience? You'll gain experience of professional creative work practices through studio-style projects, collaborative production and portfolio feedback. Our regular guest talks from industry professionals can help you build your professional network and identify work experience opportunities. You can also take part in our annual Gamebridge event, featuring industry talks, portfolio reviews, networking, showcases and recruitment activity. These experiences can help you understand professional expectations, refine how you present your work and start building your creative network. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules You’ll develop your creative voice and versatile 3D skills, preparing you to work across animation, games and emerging digital industries. Dr Adam Twycross, Senior Lecturer You'll start by building foundations in 3D animation, character creation and visual storytelling. At the same time, you'll master the essentials of real-time tools and 3D asset creation. As you progress, you’ll develop specialist interests through collaborative projects and increasingly independent practice, connecting animation with games and real-time production. Studio and experimental work gives you space to test ideas and refine your creative identity. In your final Major Project, you’ll bring your skills together in an ambitious piece of portfolio work that showcases your strengths and the direction you want to take next. What will I study? BA (Hons) With placement With foundation year BA (Hons) Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Academic Skills for Games 3D Asset Creation Character Creation Introduction to Realtime Tools Introduction to 3D Animation Year 2 Employability in Games Specialist Practice 1 Collaborative Games Development Intermediate Project for Games Ruskin Module (15 credits) Year 3 Experimental Practice Specialised Practice 2 Games Art Guided Learning Studio Practice for Games Creative Industries Major Project Module details With placement You can choose to take an optional placement year as part of this course. Placements typically happen in Year 3, and your course will take four years overall. Find out more about placement years . Placement year Work Placement - Cambridge School of Creative Industries Module details With foundation year To prepare you for university study, you can take a foundation year at the start of this course. Find out more about foundation years . Year 1 Foundation in Art and Design Module details What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. What happens on a placement year? Your placement year is a chance to put everything you’ve learnt in Years 1 and 2 into practice. Spend typically 9-12 months working for an organisation, developing your skills and gaining valuable work experience. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. Who teaches 3D Animation at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Adam Twycross Senior Lecturer Dr Barış Işıkgüner Associate Professor Amanda Surowka Lecturer Matthew Holland Lecturer Facilities You’ll create in a professional-standard environment designed to reflect the realities of the games industry. Professional-specification workstations, equipped with RTX graphics technology, give you access to powerful creative workflows, industry software, and specialist kit. Integrated studio spaces allow you to collaborate comfortably, replicating professional game studio workflows. In our dedicated communal space you can collaborate, connect, play, and relax. You’ll also benefit from access to advanced shared technical resources including motion capture, 3D prototyping, full-body scanning, and emerging AR development technologies; and training in the use of all our creative facilities , including a digital workshop with a variety of computer aided manufacturing machines. Entry requirements Standard entry requirements BA (Hons) With placement With foundation year BA (Hons) 120-104 UCAS Tariff points. We accept A Levels, T Levels, BTECs, OCR, Access to HE and most other qualifications within the UCAS Tariff. Preferably to include Psychology or a Science subject at A level or equivalent level. 3 GCSEs at grade C, or grade 4, or above, including English and Maths. If English is not your first language you will be expected to demonstrate a certificated level of proficiency of at least IELTS 6.5 ( Academic level) or equivalent English Language qualification, as recognised by Anglia Ruskin University. UCAS Tariff Points from Access to HE Diplomas in a related subject are accepted. UCAS Tariff points from the Irish Leaving Certificate are accepted. UCAS Tariff points from Scottish Advanced Highers are accepted. UCAS Tariff points acquired from BTEC Level 3 Diplomas are accepted. UCAS Tariff points from Scottish Highers are accepted. The European Baccalaureate at a minimum overall grade of 70% is accepted. International Baccalaureate Diploma with a minimum of 26 points is accepted. HNC qualifications are accepted. HND qualifications are accepted. Important additional notes Our published entry requirements are a guide only and our decision will be based on your overall suitability for the course as well as whether you meet the minimum entry requirements. Other equivalent qualifications may be accepted for entry to this course; please email [email protected] for further information. Applicants to undergraduate courses can also check our information about undergraduate entry qualifications . You'll need a computer and reliable internet access to successfully engage with your course. With placement See entry requirements for the BA or BSc (Hons) With foundation year 5 GCSEs at grade D, or grade 3, or above and evidence of two years post-GCSE study at Level 3. If you have achieved at least grade E in one A level, or equivalent, you are exempt from the two years post-GCSE study requirement, but you still must meet the GCSE requirements. Applicants who do not meet the two years post GCSE study at level 3 may be considered based on their satisfactory employment history, which must be a minimum of two years full time employment supported by employer evidence and deemed appropriate by the University for meeting the course of study applied for. If English is not your first language you will be expected to demonstrate a certificated level of proficiency of at least IELTS 5.5 (Academic level) or equivalent English Language qualification, as recognised by Anglia Ruskin University. Portfolio review You will need to send us a digital portfolio for review when you apply. For full information on how to prepare and submit your portfolio, visit our undergraduate Computer Games portfolios page . Contextual offers You can find out more about the admissions process at ARU, including what happens after you apply and the different types of offer we may make. We may automatically offer you a place at ARU if you meet any of these criteria: are a care leaver or care experienced have a declared disability are from certain postcodes provide unpaid care for another person are currently, or were, in receipt of free school meals during secondary education are a Service Child, where a parent or carer currently serves in the UK Armed Forces participated in an approved activity in preparation for entry to higher education attended a secondary school that had a Progress 8 score of average, below average or well below average Find out more about contextual offers .
